newsitem.title: GERMANY: German ministry sees rise in 1997/98 beef prices.
newsitem.headline: German ministry sees rise in 1997/98 beef prices.

text.p: Prices of German cow beef in 1997/98 (July/June) are forecast to rise by five to 10 percent over 1996/97, the Bonn agriculture ministry said in a weekly market report.
Prices of bullock beef should also be slightly higher than the year before, it said, citing a panel of experts.
The price increases would correspond with a fall in slaughter levels by five percent over 1996/97 to 4.6 million animals and small reductions in consumption.
At European Union level, the 1997/98 forecast was for a slight rise in consumption along with a fall in slaughterings by two to three percent.
The experts also said EU prices should fall in the medium term as a result of surplus stocks.
German prices of beef for slaughter in 1996/97 were an average 6.9 percent down from 1995/96 as a result of the mad cow disease which turned consumers off beef.
But prices started to recover in the second quarter of 1997.
Prices per kilo slaughter weight in 1996/97 were 4.32 marks compared with 4.64 marks in 1995/96 and 5.22 in 1994/95.
Germany at an end-June livestock count had 15.63 million cattle, 2.1 percent less than a year earlier.
